name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3261
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email November 14, 2012 This article appears in the December 3, 2012 issue.

clue.text: Word such as "wine" or "water"—or "transubstantiation"?

blocks.note: first meaning: the grammatical term for an uncountable word such as these
second meaning: a word belonging to the Catholic Eucharist service

explanation.walkthrough: Wine and water cannot be counted; transubstantiation is the doctrine that bread and wine become Christ's body and blood during the Eucharist, so it is a word of that service.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call uncountable nouns like wine and water by this term, and the pun reads it as a word from the church service.

clue.text: Something good but confusing — viz: math

indicators.note: something confusing is jumbled up, so the letters after the colon are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Mathematics is said to be beneficial yet baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish usage a mitzvah is a commandment, and colloquially any good deed or act of kindness.

clue.text: Track from satisfactory to unsatisfactory

blocks.note: S is the school grade for satisfactory
poor means not good enough

explanation.surface: A running track deteriorates from acceptable to substandard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from X to Y' reads like a decline in quality, but it simply sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of footprints or droppings left by an animal, followed by hunters.

clue.text: Auditory realignment: outside of North Carolina, everybody supposedly gets one

indicators.note: a realignment puts things into a new order, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go on the outside, wrapping around the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the US postal abbreviation for the state

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hearing correction, with a North Carolina aside about what everyone is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the right to be heard by a court is supposed to be universal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a fair hearing before a judge, a chance proverbially owed to every person.

clue.text: Musician lacking first aid

indicators.note: lacking its first means the opening letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: a bass player

explanation.surface: A performer goes without basic medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' reads as a phrase, but 'first' belongs to the deletion and 'aid' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, the verb sense of aid.

clue.text: Business attempt at the foot of Asian river

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot is the bottom, so the attempt is placed after the river

blocks.note: the Indus flows through Pakistan
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to start a company at the mouth of a river in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means commercial activity or a branch of trade, as business does.

clue.text: Walk within legal limits

blocks.note: first meaning: a stroll taken for one's health
second meaning: permitted by a nation's founding law

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests strolling within bounds; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it names a healthful daily stroll; as an adjective it means in accordance with the national charter.

clue.text: Otherwise neutral, Asner is just the same

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different form, so the next word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
Ed Asner was the American actor who played Lou Grant

explanation.surface: Apart from taking sides, the actor hasn't changed a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Asner, star of The Mary Tyler Moore Show and Lou Grant, is clued by surname to give his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaltered has not changed at all, remaining identical.

clue.text: Welcomed neatnik after tidying up

indicators.note: tidying up rearranges things, so the preceding word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fastidious person is greeted once the cleaning is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken in is to be received as a guest or given shelter.

clue.text: Cocktail's mixed-in asset: liqueur

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the following words' letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bartender praises a drink whose stirred-in strength is a liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: This mixed drink of tequila, orange juice and grenadine is named for its sunset-like layers.

clue.text: Bargains with lunatic, softer on the exterior

indicators.note: a lunatic arrangement is a crazy one, so the following word's letters are scrambled
the scrambled letters sit on the outside, enclosing the single letter from the clue's first link

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up deals alongside a madman who is gentler on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: TWOFERS is an American colloquialism for two-for-one offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A twofer is a deal giving two items for the price of one, so these are cut-price offers.

clue.text: Evangelist pursues hiding place for The Nation

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the evangelist is placed second

blocks.note: a den is a lair or secret retreat
Mark is one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.surface: A preacher chases down a secret spot to serve The Nation, the magazine running this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Nation' looks like the magazine's own name; only 'Nation' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: In retrospective, Picasso's outrivaled masters of technique

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them
a retrospective looks backward, so the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the painter's name with its possessive, then the start of the next word

explanation.surface: An art critic says that in a Picasso retrospective, his works outshone the great technicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosos are performers or artists of supreme technical skill.

clue.text: Giant clamp on the tongue

indicators.note: something on the tongue is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to clamp something is to tighten it

explanation.surface: A huge device seems to grip someone's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the gigantic deities of Greek myth, and the word now means any colossus.

clue.text: Smoking near pillow's center in lodges

indicators.note: near means right beside, so the two parts are simply set next to each other

blocks.note: something smoking is very hot
the middle of pillow is a pair of the letter L, and that letter written out is el, so two of them are els

explanation.surface: Someone lights up near the middle of a pillow in a lodge, a fire hazard in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters are not lifted as they stand: the pair of Ls is written out as the letter's name, el, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels and lodges are both places offering travellers paid rooms for the night.

clue.text: Could this be a source of financial independence? Sounds like bondage play would

definitions.text: Could this be a source of financial independence?

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: being tied up for fun

explanation.surface: A wry question about where money comes from, followed by a cheeky remark about tying people up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays against the surface: bondage is the opposite of independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Money held in trust can give an heir an income without working, the classic route to being financially self-sufficient.

clue.text: 3.0 (three) crackers held by nurse's colleagues

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the bracketed number word is jumbled
something held by another thing is inside it, so the jumble goes within the nurse

blocks.note: a 3.0 grade point average is a B in US schools
RN is a registered nurse
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Three crackers are being passed round by a nurse's coworkers, with an oddly precise 3.0.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition. A 3.0 GPA is a straight B average in American grading.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren is an old plural of brother used for fellow members of a profession, church or society.

clue.text: They help you go down fast and pass over shouts of encouragement

definitions.text: They help you go down fast

blocks.note: to skip is to pass over or omit
the bullfight cheer, plural

explanation.surface: Spectators cheering on someone hurtling downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers push off and balance with these sticks while speeding down a slope.

clue.text: Chilled dessert, for the most part, sometimes referred to as a meat dish

indicators.note: most of something means all but its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a light, cold, whipped pudding
AKA, also known as, introduces another name

explanation.surface: A cold pudding is mostly what people call, oddly, a meat course.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of minced lamb layered with aubergine and sauce.

clue.text: Exploit to frighten farm animal

blocks.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
to cow is to intimidate

explanation.surface: Someone plans to take advantage of livestock by scaring it.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk cow is a dairy cow, kept on a farm for its milk.

clue.text: Rewind parts of an inning I'd seen inside TV station

indicators.note: what is seen inside something sits within it, so the short pronoun goes into the baseball term
rewinding runs a tape backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a baseball half-inning ends after three outs
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A baseball fan wants a replay of the bits of an inning they watched at the broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room or building where television programmes are made and broadcast.

clue.text: Go on — act crazy with a stop sign, e.g.

indicators.note: crazy signals disorder, so the words before it are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to behave wildly while waving a traffic sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop sign is the familiar example of an eight-sided shape.

clue.text: Speaker's false takeover is a puzzle

indicators.note: a speaker's version is the spoken one, so the following words are judged by sound

blocks.note: pseudo means false and a coup is a seizure of power

explanation.surface: A parliamentary Speaker calls a bogus seizure of power baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is the number-placement grid game, filling a nine-by-nine square.

clue.text: "Orcuspay" language?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nonsense word from the schoolyard code that moves an opening consonant to the end and adds 'ay'
setter's reading: undo the code to get porcus, the classical Romans' word for a pig, so its tongue is the one wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Orcuspay is Pig Latin for porcus, which is Latin for pig: a word that is literally pig Latin twice over. The answer is the language of porcus.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical tongue of ancient Rome, in which porcus is the ordinary word for a swine.

clue.text: Underworld figure and stoolie hold $100 for powerful magnate

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the money sits within the informer

blocks.note: the Roman god of the underworld
C is the Roman numeral for 100, and a C-note is a hundred-dollar bill
a stool pigeon or informer is a rat

explanation.surface: A gangster and an informant pocket a hundred-dollar bill for a mogul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a mobster, which suits the surface; here it is the god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power derives from great wealth, a rich and influential tycoon.

clue.text: One sporting frightful horn!

indicators.note: frightful suggests a mess, so the following word is jumbled
sporting means wearing, so the jumbled word carries the numeral within it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An exclamation at some creature wearing a scary horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: the beast is defined by its fearsome horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is the large animal famous for the horn or horns on its snout.

clue.text: Key group of spies supplants Egypt's leader in inflicting pain

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the country's opening letter is taken
to supplant is to take another's place, so the spy agency replaces that letter

blocks.note: cruel means causing suffering
the first letter of the country name
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A crucial spy ring ousts an Egyptian ruler by torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key group' tempts a musical chord or a set of islands; 'Key' alone is the definition. The CIA takes the place of the E in a word for causing pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something key is of decisive importance, which is what crucial means.

clue.text: Zero grade for speechifying

blocks.note: zero resembles the letter O
a rating is a grade or score

explanation.surface: A judge awards nothing to a long-winded speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal, often pompous speech, which is what speechifying describes.

clue.text: Married gays, initially, beginning to educate children!

definitions.text: Married gays, initially, beginning to educate children!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of the verb that follows

blocks.note: to wed is to marry
first letter of the word
first letter of the word
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: A scandalised cry about same-sex couples marrying and then teaching kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: in 2012 American politics, gay marriage and what schools teach children were classic examples of divisive campaign topics.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge issue is a divisive political topic used to split an opponent's supporters, as same-sex marriage was in US elections.
